data.cultural_impact: The name Ravina may evoke sentiments of brilliance, illumination, and prosperity, as the "Ravi" part of the name can be derived from the Sanskrit word "Ravi," meaning "sun." Sun is considered the source of energy and light, and therefore, the name Ravina can imply a deep connection to power, authority, and illumination. In Indian culture, there are several deities or gods associated with the sun, such as Surya or Ravi, and they are considered to have the power to benevolently illuminate and nourish all around them. This name could symbolize an individual who is at the center of lives, providing warmth, energy, and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, Ravina could be seen as an embodiment of divine light and consciousness. The vibration and energies of this name may bring spiritual awakening, self-realization, and inner illumination. The "Rav" part can be connected to the Sanskrit word "Rasa," which means "juice, essence, taste, and that wherein all desires melt away," symbolizing the pure essence that can be found within us all. The "ina" part may be linked to the Sanskrit words "vin" (conquer) and "asana" (seat or position), implying the power to occupy or conquer the inner self and assume a divine position within an individual's being. From this perspective, Ravina represents the triumph of the eternal inner light over the transient physical world and is a reminder of our infinite potential for growth, transformation, and spiritual enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Ravana, the King of Lanka in Hindu mythology, was a great demon king and an adversary of Rama, the hero of the ‘Ramayana’ epic. He abducted Sita, Rama’s wife, and was eventually killed by Rama in a great battle.

Another interpretation of Ravana comes from the Puranic literature, where he is described as a great sage and a devotee of Lord Shiva. He is also said to have built the magnificent temple of Lord Rama at Rameswaram.

modern_usage.modern_context: Ravina is a name that has its roots in Hindu mythology and has seen modern usage across various platforms. In movies, Ravina Saini was a character portrayed by Preity Zinta in the film 'Singh is King' released in 2006. The name Ravina was also used in the TV series 'The Legend of Ravina' which aired in 2018. In literature, 'Ravina's Lament' is a novel by Revathy Ashlock published in 2019. The name Ravina has become popular in various forms of media, especially in fantasy literature and character names. It is a unisex name, and its usage in modern contexts shows a trend towards incorporating rich cultural heritage into contemporary stories and characters.

name_in_real_life.story: Priya Ravina, a teacher in Bangalore, India, shares that their name Ravina meaning "Jewel, treasure" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ravina, meaning 'night reveler' or 'night delight', symbolizes the inner awakening to embrace the unknown, mystery, and darkness within oneself. It is a name that encourages exploration of the hidden depths, where wisdom and Self-realization can be discovered.
